latency.status: implemented and measured in three isolated paired runs; final latest-version interactions verified in repeat probes
latency.interpretation: In three paired 40-edit bursts, successful hover/completion P95 improves from about 899–912ms to 737–754ms. Update work drops; queue latency was not the bottleneck. No navigation speedup claim: subsequent edits cancel 31–35 old definition requests, consistent with RA NO_RETRY policy. Latest-version hover/completion/definition all return usable results after each repeat.
latency.implementation: file_fixities reads only top-level fixity declarations from semantic CST; input updates no longer force full ItemTree lowering and generated expansion.
limitations: Synthetic burst client timings include backlog; not a single-keystroke or Zed SSH latency claim.
Three repetitions on one host do not establish a universal performance guarantee.
Do not compare cancelled definition response durations as successful navigation latency.

cache_experiment.decision: Rejected and reverted: final sweep 969 MiB vs 734 MiB; final sweep reached at 203815 ms vs 152405 ms. Reloads returned heap to 742 MiB but did not justify throughput regression.
cache_experiment.policy: Retain 512-entry per-callable body/source-map caches and weak parse seeds. Preserve expensive inference results. Do not cap raw/semantic parses at 128; investigate query ownership/recomputation before another cap. Finite project sweep reaches plateau, not a proof of global boundedness.
